feedback.actual_behavior: The child receives inherited history or no applicable plan contract.
feedback.expected_behavior: Resolve project-first contract and supply only bounded slice, goal and gates with clean context.
feedback.invariant: Optional plans preserve existing SOW routing, project authority, and evidence-backed acceptance.

scenarios.request: Delegate one approved child SOW.
scenarios.context: The canonical contract is resolved and dependency gates pass.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Supply accessible applicable contract, G#, exact scope and gates in a self-contained task; coordinator verifies handoff.
scenarios.must_not: Copy the template into the consumer skill or delegate overlapping scope.

scenarios.request: Delegate plan work to a native custom agent.
scenarios.context: Parent conversation includes unrelated requests and reviews.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use fork_turns none and only task-local inputs; retain coordinator ownership.
scenarios.must_not: Use fork_turns all or attach historical chat.

scenarios.request: Delegate standalone SOW implementation.
scenarios.context: No parent plan exists; approved exact SOW coverage is available.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Delegate the bounded SOW without requiring plan or G#; preserve isolation and local verification.
scenarios.must_not: Block unrelated execution for missing plan owner or auto-install it.

feedback.trigger: A user asks to delegate a task, SOW, or plan to GLM5.2 after adding that native Codex sub-agent.
feedback.actual_behavior: The skill routes work through a Claude CLI session, logs, and parser instead of the requested native sub-agent.
feedback.expected_behavior: Select the registered GLM5.2 native sub-agent, preserve SOW-first controls, and independently review the result.
feedback.invariant: Explicit delegate-model requests use the requested available native sub-agent without a silent provider fallback.

scenarios.request: Delegate this approved SOW to GLM5.2.
scenarios.context: The SOW has explicit write scope and verification criteria; GLM5.2 is registered as a native sub-agent.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Spawn the GLM5.2 sub-agent with fork_turns none, the SOW path, and bounded ownership, then review and verify locally.
scenarios.must_not: Invoke Claude CLI, create Claude logs, substitute another model, or pass parent turns with fork_turns all.

scenarios.request: Implement this approved SOW locally.
scenarios.context: The user does not request delegation or name a sub-agent.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the normal execution flow without spawning a delegate.
scenarios.must_not: Activate delegation merely because a SOW exists.

scenarios.request: Delegate this draft plan to GLM5.2.
scenarios.context: The plan is not approved and the request is for investigation and SOW drafting only.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Allow scoped inspection or plan drafting, but prohibit product-code changes until an approved SOW exists.
scenarios.must_not: Authorize implementation work from the unapproved plan.

feedback.trigger: A native sub-agent completes delegated work and the coordinator decides whether the task can close.
feedback.actual_behavior: The coordinator can accept one local check, while approval wording conflicts with pre-approval planning delegation and the GLM role is treated as globally fixed.
feedback.expected_behavior: Gate only implementation on SOW approval, resolve the requested agent from the current catalog, and independently complete runtime verification plus gap-finding.
feedback.invariant: Native delegation preserves model intent, authorization boundaries, clean task context, and the same verification standard as local execution.

scenarios.request: Delegate this approved async UI SOW to GLM5.2 and finish it.
scenarios.context: The current agent catalog exposes a GLM5.2 custom role and the delegate reports implementation complete.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Spawn the catalog-resolved GLM5.2 role with fork_turns none, then require a multi-step runtime scenario, evidence against the SOW lock, and a gap-finding pass before closeout.
scenarios.must_not: Treat delegate completion, syntax checks, one generic local check, or inherited parent turns as task completion evidence.

scenarios.request: Delegate investigation and draft a SOW for this issue.
scenarios.context: No approved implementation SOW exists and the delegated scope is read-only analysis plus planning documentation.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Allow the planning delegation while prohibiting implementation writes.
scenarios.must_not: Reject all delegation before approval or authorize product-code changes.

scenarios.request: Delegate this approved SOW to GLM5.2.
scenarios.context: GLM5.2 is requested but its previously known role name is absent from the current agent catalog.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Resolve any currently registered GLM5.2 role; if none exists, report unavailability without substitution.
scenarios.must_not: Use a stale hardcoded role or silently delegate to another model.

feedback.trigger: Delegate a read-only review to an available agent.
feedback.actual_behavior: The entrypoint references an external repository rule file absent from skill-only installs.

scenarios.request: Delegate a read-only review to an available agent.
scenarios.context: Only the delegate skill directory is installed.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use packaged instructions and concise communication.
scenarios.must_not: Depend on an external brief-execution file.

scenarios.request: Read the delegation instructions.
scenarios.context: No historical rules folder exists.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Explain the bounded handoff without missing-file dependencies.
scenarios.must_not: Install legacy rules.

scenarios.request: Delegate from an arbitrary skills root.
scenarios.context: Project policy exists separately.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use local skill resources and respect project policy.
scenarios.must_not: Overwrite project policy.

feedback.trigger: A user asks to delegate a task to a custom agent that is not exposed as a native Codex sub-agent.
feedback.actual_behavior: The delegate flow only defines the native Codex lifecycle and does not require a new external provider session, so an old task conversation or session could be reused.
feedback.expected_behavior: Classify transport first; native agents use the native lifecycle, while every new logical task delegated to a non-native custom agent starts a fresh provider or CLI session with no old task history.
feedback.invariant: Non-native custom delegation never reuses a prior task session or historical chat; same-task continuation is explicitly bounded to the fresh session created for that task.

scenarios.request: Delegate this approved SOW to an external custom agent through its CLI.
scenarios.context: The agent is not in the native Codex catalog and the provider documents a new-session mechanism.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Initialize a unique fresh provider session, send a self-contained bounded prompt, and return session lifecycle plus verification evidence to the coordinator.
scenarios.must_not: Resume or continue an old task session, attach historical chat, or pass a prior transcript.

scenarios.request: Delegate this approved SOW to native GLM5.2.
scenarios.context: The current native agent catalog exposes the registered GLM5.2 role.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the native `spawn_agent` lifecycle with fork_turns none and keep the coordinator's independent review gates.
scenarios.must_not: Create an external CLI session, pass fork_turns all, or treat a native child as a non-native agent.

scenarios.request: Send a follow-up after the external custom agent asks a question.
scenarios.context: The follow-up belongs to the same logical task and the just-created fresh session identity remains provable.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Continue only that fresh task session with the minimum approved clarification; if history is compacted, stale, or uncertain, start another fresh session with a concise handoff.
scenarios.must_not: Silently attach an older task conversation or reuse a session whose task identity cannot be proved.

feedback.trigger: Substantive execution or review enters this delegation flow with model selection open.
feedback.actual_behavior: The delegation flow can skip exact GLM-5.3-max, reuse a stale session, or hide a failed handoff behind local continuation.
feedback.expected_behavior: When exact greennode/glm-5.3 with reasoning_effort=max is available and a safe bounded slice exists, delegate it first; preserve explicit overrides, fresh context, evidence-backed fallback, and cleanup.
feedback.invariant: Mandatory GLM-5.3-max delegation is exact-model evidenced, context-isolated, coordinator-owned, and never a silent alternate-model or old-session path.

scenarios.request: Delegate a bounded review of this approved SOW without naming a model.
scenarios.context: The current catalog exposes exact greennode/glm-5.3 with max reasoning; native transport is available.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Select the exact target, start the native child with fork_turns none, return model, transport, availability, lifecycle, isolation, and coordinator verification evidence, then clean up.
scenarios.must_not: Choose GLM-5.3 Flash, GLM5.2, or pass parent turns into the child.

scenarios.request: Delegate this review to the explicitly selected native GLM5.2 role.
scenarios.context: The user explicitly names GLM5.2, which is a valid model override for this invocation.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Honor the explicit GLM5.2 choice and keep the coordinator responsible for verification and cleanup.
scenarios.must_not: Override the explicit target with GLM-5.3-max or pass parent turns into the child.

scenarios.request: Attempt delegation when exact GLM-5.3-max is unavailable, or after a launch failure, runtime failure, isolation failure, or invalid delegate output.
scenarios.context: Current catalog evidence says the exact target is unavailable; a separate handoff has a failed stage after bounded repair and a non-native candidate has an old session.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Record the unavailable or failed stage, discard invalid delegate output, clean up failed task-owned sessions, and use local fallback only in automatic mode; explicit delegation stops and asks.
scenarios.must_not: Fallback to GLM5.2 or Flash silently, reuse old task history, spawn a nested child, or treat failure as success.

feedback.trigger: Approved task execution enters the named automatic-execution-delegation mode after its mandatory exact-model availability gate.
feedback.actual_behavior: The delegate skill rejects the internal caller as ordinary single-agent work or applies explicit-delegation fallback rules to a mandatory automatic handoff.
feedback.expected_behavior: Accept only the execution flow's internal mode, preserve the bounded SOW slice and isolation contract, and return confirmed unavailable or failed checks to the coordinator for evidence-backed local fallback.
feedback.invariant: Internal automatic delegation is a narrowly authorized composition path; explicit user delegation remains stop/ask and never silently substitutes a model or session.

scenarios.request: Start the approved slice through task-execution-flow's automatic-execution-delegation mode.
scenarios.context: The execution flow has confirmed a bounded, non-secret slice and supplied the SOW path, availability evidence, mandatory delegation decision, and local verification plan.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Accept the internal mode, apply exact GLM-5.3-max routing and fresh-context rules, and return handoff plus lifecycle evidence to the coordinator.
scenarios.must_not: Treat the call as an unbounded delegation, bypass the SOW, or reuse parent history.

scenarios.request: Run ordinary single-agent execution while merely mentioning another model, without the internal automatic mode.
scenarios.context: No explicit user delegation and no task-execution mandatory availability decision is present.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Do not activate the delegate flow; an explicit user delegation, when actually requested, continues through the existing explicit path.
scenarios.must_not: Infer automatic delegation from a model mention or broaden the public trigger implicitly.

scenarios.request: Enter automatic-execution-delegation when exact GLM-5.3-max, a compatible transport, or fresh isolation is unavailable; separately handle an explicit user delegation to that unavailable target.
scenarios.context: Current catalog or transport evidence identifies the failed availability or isolation check; the automatic slice may continue coordinator-only, but explicit delegation has no safe substitute.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Return the exact failed check to task-execution-flow for local continuation in automatic mode; stop and ask for explicit delegation without selecting another model or old session.
scenarios.must_not: Guess a variant match, resume historical context, or silently turn explicit delegation into local execution.

feedback.trigger: A review or independent-review sub-agent is still running when the coordinator is ready to clean up delegation.
feedback.actual_behavior: The lifecycle can interrupt an idle or active review delegate immediately without a bounded wait for its findings.
feedback.expected_behavior: Wait up to ten minutes for a running or unresolved-idle review delegate, then make an explicit cut decision; terminal results may be cleaned up immediately.
feedback.invariant: Review evidence is protected by a bounded ten-minute grace period, while completed delegates and implementation delegates retain their existing cleanup behavior.

scenarios.request: Run an independent review and keep the reviewer alive while it is still working.
scenarios.context: The native review sub-agent is running and has not returned findings or a question.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Wait in bounded increments for at most ten minutes and do not call interrupt_agent immediately.
scenarios.must_not: Cut the running reviewer at the end of the coordinator's current turn or report missing findings as complete.

scenarios.request: Clean up a review sub-agent that has returned a terminal result.
scenarios.context: The final status and review output have already been read.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Clean up the task-owned child without an artificial ten-minute delay.
scenarios.must_not: Wait ten minutes after a confirmed terminal result or interrupt an unrelated task.

scenarios.request: The review sub-agent is still running after ten minutes.
scenarios.context: No final result, question, or failure is available; the coordinator must choose whether to keep waiting or cut.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Report the unchanged state, make an explicit cut/keep decision, and mark a cut review incomplete/unverified.
scenarios.must_not: Silently cut the reviewer, claim the review completed, or wait without a decision boundary.

feedback.trigger: Delegate an explicitly selected Claude Code review or implementation task.
feedback.actual_behavior: The agent guesses a Claude CLI model, resumes a prior session, or treats stream-json output as completion without checking the resolved model and repository result.
feedback.expected_behavior: Use the documented fresh claude -p transport, route analytical work to opus and approved implementation to sonnet, inspect the init model and terminal result, then let the coordinator verify locally.
feedback.invariant: External Claude delegation is fresh, model-specific, bounded by approval, and never substitutes transport or coordinator verification silently.

scenarios.request: Run an explicitly selected Claude review of a known SOW.
scenarios.context: The task is read-only; the Claude CLI is available and the init event resolves opus at high effort.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Start a fresh claude -p process with no persistence, plan mode and bounded read tools; parse stream-json and return the advisory result for coordinator verification.
scenarios.must_not: Use --continue or --resume, pass parent history, or treat the delegate result as final approval.

scenarios.request: Delegate to Claude when the requested alias is unavailable or the init event resolves a different model.
scenarios.context: The CLI returns an availability error or a model identity mismatch before the result can be trusted.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Record the concrete failure, discard the handoff, and stop or follow the existing evidence-backed fallback rule without silent substitution.
scenarios.must_not: Switch to another Claude model, resume an old session, or report a valid handoff.

scenarios.request: Implement an approved code slice through explicitly selected Claude Code.
scenarios.context: The SOW names the exact write scope and verification; the init event resolves sonnet at high effort, while a destructive production action remains separately gated.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use acceptEdits with approved file tools only, preserve the destructive safety gate, and let the coordinator inspect the diff and run verification.
scenarios.must_not: Edit outside the SOW, use dangerously-skip-permissions, or remove required safety approval.
